corrections.claimed_speedup: Tessil hash-table-shootout, from the raw results CSV linked from the page (the page itself shows charts): read_random_full at n=3,000,000: std::unordered_map 0.297209 s vs google::dense_hash_map 0.054073 s (~5.5x, derived from page data); insert_random_full at n=3,000,000: 1.055850 s vs 0.308572 s (~3.4x, derived from page data). Across all tests and sizes, dense_hash_map is faster in 20 of 21 tests with a ~2.3x overall geometric-mean speedup (derived from page data); per-test geomeans range from 0.90x (insert_string) to 13.05x (delete_random_full) (derived from page data).
corrections.caveats: The page says integer tests use libstdc++'s identity std::hash for all maps. dense_hash_map loses on insert_string (0.90x, derived from page data), and the page notes it does poorly on read misses relative to other open-addressing maps and needs more memory at high load factors.

Parallel: the paper reports no parallel speedup against std::sort; its parallel speedups (8.37 on A1x16, 40.92 on A1x64, 20.91 on I4x20, 17.49 on I2x16) are relative to sequential I1S4o.
